intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the rainforest canopy on a thrilling multi-cable zip-line circuit with stunning views of Arenal Volcano. Experience the cloud forest ecosystem from above while spotting toucans, howler monkeys, and sloths along the way. Most operators include a hanging bridges walk as part of the package.
experiences.location: La Fortuna, Arenal Volcano National Park

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari, spotting caimans, river turtles, poison dart frogs, manatees, and an extraordinary variety of tropical birds. If visiting between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of endangered green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Night Walk
experiences.description: Explore the mystical Monteverde Cloud Forest after dark with a naturalist guide who uses spotlights to reveal nocturnal wildlife including kinkajous, glass frogs, tarantulas, sleeping birds, and the elusive olingo. The cloud forest takes on an entirely different character at night and offers a truly unforgettable eco-adventure experience.
experiences.location: Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve, Puntarenas Province

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio Beach and Rainforest Combo Day
experiences.description: Spend a day in Manuel Antonio National Park where pristine white-sand beaches meet lush rainforest teeming with wildlife. Spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, three-toed sloths, and scarlet macaws just steps from the turquoise Pacific waters. Hire a local guide for two hours to maximize wildlife sightings, then relax on Playa Manuel Antonio afterward.

experiences.name: Cacao Farm Tour and Traditional Costa Rican Cooking Class
experiences.description: Visit a working organic cacao farm to learn the full bean-to-bar chocolate-making process used by indigenous Bribri communities for centuries. Follow the tour with a hands-on cooking class preparing traditional Costa Rican dishes such as gallo pinto, casado, and plantain-based recipes using locally sourced ingredients. A rich cultural and culinary immersion in one experience.
experiences.location: Puerto Viejo de Talamanca, Caribbean South Coast

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange budget shuttle transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort on the beachfront (shared shuttle services like Interbus or Caribe Shuttle are affordable options). Check in, freshen up, and take a relaxed stroll along the beach to get your bearings and soak in your first Costa Rican sunset views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the immediate beachfront area near the resort on foot. Visit the local sodas (small family-run eateries) nearby for an authentic and affordable first dinner. Watch the sunset from the beach and decompress from travel.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport or on the plane before arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable casado (rice, beans, meat, salad) at a soda near the airport or on the road to the resort (~$5-8 USD)
meals.dinner: Dine at a local soda near the resort - try gallo pinto, fried plantains, and fresh fish (~$6-10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is purely arrival and settling in. Keep spending minimal. Exchange some cash to colones at the airport for better rates. Confirm your itinerary plans and ask resort staff for budget tips.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and enjoy the beachfront sunrise. Take a self-guided walk along the beach to spot wildlife such as pelicans, frigate birds, and possibly howler monkeys in nearby trees. Pack a light snack and hydrate well.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby national park or wildlife reserve accessible from the resort area. Explore walking trails independently (entrance fees for national parks are ~$18 USD for foreigners but offer incredible value). Look for sloths, iguanas, and tropical birds along the trails.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and relax on the beach. Head to a local beachfront restaurant for a casual dinner and enjoy the warm evening air.

meals.breakfast: Fruit, bread, and coffee at a local bakery or resort café (~$3-5 USD)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from a local market - fresh fruit, bread, and snacks (~$4-6 USD)
meals.dinner: Beachfront soda with fresh ceviche and rice and beans (~$8-12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear reef-safe sunscreen, bring insect repellent, and carry a reusable water bottle. National park trails are best explored in the morning when wildlife is most active.

day_by_day.morning: Book a budget zip-lining tour through a local operator near the resort area. Many companies offer half-day zip-line adventures through the rainforest canopy at prices ranging from $45-75 USD. Zip-lining is one of Costa Rica's signature eco-adventure experiences and offers stunning aerial views of the jungle.
day_by_day.afternoon: After zip-lining, visit a local butterfly garden or frog sanctuary nearby - these are often inexpensive (~$10-15 USD) and offer incredible wildlife viewing opportunities. Spot poison dart frogs, morpho butterflies, and other exotic species up close.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a well-earned rest back at the resort. Walk along the beach at dusk to spot nesting or feeding shorebirds. Cook or buy simple street food for a budget-friendly dinner.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto (rice and beans) with eggs and fresh juice at a local soda (~$4-6 USD)
meals.lunch: Light snack at the zip-line tour base camp or nearby sodas (~$5-8 USD)
meals.dinner: Street food tacos or empanadas from a local vendor (~$4-7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book zip-lining in advance or through your resort to avoid peak-time price hikes. Wear closed-toe shoes and comfortable clothes. Most operators provide helmets and harnesses.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning wildlife walk or guided bird-watching tour. Costa Rica is home to over 900 bird species, making it a paradise for birders. Budget guides can be found locally for ~$20-30 USD per person and are well worth the investment for spotting toucans, macaws, and hummingbirds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local farmers market or mercado to browse fresh tropical fruits, handmade crafts, and local products. This is a great way to engage with local culture and pick up affordable souvenirs. Try fresh coconut water, mangoes, and star fruit.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local town or village near the resort. Visit the central plaza, observe daily life, and find a budget-friendly restaurant for dinner. Try a traditional casado plate.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruit plate and coffee at the market (~$3-5 USD)
meals.lunch: Casado lunch at a local soda - includes rice, beans, salad, protein, and drink (~$6-9 USD)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant with traditional Costa Rican cuisine (~$8-12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: February is dry season in many parts of Costa Rica, making it ideal for outdoor activities. Carry cash as many local vendors and sodas do not accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to a nearby waterfall or natural swimming hole. Many are accessible by local bus or shared taxi for minimal cost. Bring a swimsuit, water shoes, and a dry bag. Enjoy a refreshing swim in the natural pool at the base of the waterfall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the surrounding jungle trails near the waterfall independently. Look for wildlife such as coatis, howler monkeys, and colorful frogs. Take photos and enjoy the lush biodiversity of the rainforest.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by local bus or shared shuttle. Relax on the beach and enjoy the evening. Cook a simple meal using ingredients from the local market to save money.

meals.breakfast: Homemade or resort breakfast with gallo pinto and fresh juice (~$3-5 USD)
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from local market ingredients - sandwiches, fruit, and snacks (~$4-6 USD)
meals.dinner: Self-prepared simple meal or affordable soda dinner (~$5-8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Waterfall trails can be slippery - wear proper footwear. Always hike with a buddy or inform someone of your plans. Check local bus schedules in advance to plan return trips.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at the beach enjoying the waves and natural surroundings. Try snorkeling if equipment rental is available locally (~$10-15 USD) to explore the underwater marine life, including tropical fish and coral reefs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local wildlife rescue center or animal sanctuary. These facilities rehabilitate injured and orphaned animals like sloths, monkeys, and birds. Entry fees (~$15-25 USD) directly support conservation efforts and offer incredible close-up wildlife encounters.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset beach walk followed by dinner at a beachfront restaurant. Try arroz con mariscos (seafood rice) or fresh grilled fish, which are often very affordable at local spots.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes or toast with fresh tropical jam at a local café (~$4-6 USD)
meals.lunch: Fresh ceviche and patacones (fried plantains) at a beachside vendor (~$6-9 USD)
meals.dinner: Grilled fish with rice and salad at a beachfront soda (~$9-13 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Choose wildlife rescue centers that are certified and ethical. Avoid venues that allow riding or excessive handling of animals. Ask resort staff for reputable recommendations.

day_by_day.morning: Take a guided mangrove kayaking tour if available near the resort area. Mangrove ecosystems are incredibly biodiverse and kayaking through them offers close encounters with birds, crocodiles, and monkeys. Budget tours start at ~$30-50 USD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest and recharge at the resort. Use the afternoon to plan the second half of your trip, do laundry, and review your budget. Explore the resort grounds and nearby beachfront areas.
day_by_day.evening: Socialize with fellow travelers at the resort or a nearby hostel common area. Share travel tips and stories. Enjoy a low-key dinner at a nearby soda.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto with eggs and fresh orange juice (~$4-6 USD)
meals.lunch: Snack at the kayak tour base or pack your own (~$4-7 USD)
meals.dinner: Budget soda dinner with casado and a local beer (~$7-10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Midpoint of the trip - a great time to reassess your budget and spending. Look for free or low-cost activities for the remaining days if needed. Wash and dry gear for upcoming adventures.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to a nearby national park or reserve you haven't visited yet. Explore the trails early in the morning for the best wildlife sightings. Look for white-faced capuchin monkeys, coatis, sloths, and an array of tropical birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the national park or reserve. Find a shaded spot near a river or lagoon for a peaceful picnic lunch. Keep an eye out for caimans, turtles, and herons near water sources.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and enjoy a relaxing evening on the beach. Try stargazing from the beach as February skies in Costa Rica are often clear during the dry season.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at a local soda before heading out (~$4-6 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch from the local market (~$4-6 USD)
meals.dinner: Fresh fish tacos or a simple meal at a local restaurant (~$7-11 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Bring binoculars for wildlife viewing - they make a huge difference for bird watching. Apply insect repellent before entering forested areas. Stay on marked trails.

day_by_day.morning: Try a morning yoga or meditation session on the beach (many resorts or local instructors offer free or low-cost sessions). Alternatively, take an early morning jog along the beach and collect shells or observe shorebird feeding behavior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local chocolate or coffee tour if available in the region (~$15-25 USD). Costa Rica is famous for its high-quality cacao and coffee, and these tours offer fascinating insight into the production process with tastings included.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local cultural event, live music performance, or community gathering if available. Many beach towns have free evening entertainment. Enjoy a casual dinner with new friends.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or fruit plate at a health café (~$4-7 USD)
meals.lunch: Lunch at the chocolate or coffee tour facility (~$5-8 USD)
meals.dinner: Shared meal at a local restaurant with fellow travelers (~$8-12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Look for free community events, beach bonfires, or open-air movie nights in nearby towns. These offer authentic cultural experiences at no cost.

day_by_day.morning: Take a guided night hike or early morning hike to spot nocturnal wildlife such as tree frogs, tarantulas, and bats. Many local guides offer budget night tours (~$20-35 USD) that are both thrilling and educational.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a leisurely afternoon at the beach swimming, sunbathing, and relaxing. Rent a surfboard or bodyboard if available locally (~$10-15 USD per hour) and try catching some waves.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner to celebrate being in Costa Rica. Try a restaurant that specializes in traditional Tico cuisine with fresh local ingredients. Toast to your adventure.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the resort or a local café (~$5-8 USD)
meals.lunch: Beach snacks - fresh coconut, fruit, and empanadas from vendors (~$4-6 USD)
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer traditional restaurant (~$12-18 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Night hikes require a reliable flashlight or headlamp. Follow the guide's instructions carefully and stay on the path. This is one of the most memorable wildlife experiences in Costa Rica.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby hot spring or natural thermal pool if accessible from the resort area. Many hot springs in Costa Rica are free or low-cost when accessed through public entry points rather than luxury resorts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a self-guided hike to a scenic viewpoint or mirador with panoramic views of the coastline, jungle, or volcanic landscape. Bring a camera and plenty of water for the hike.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a local cooking class or food demonstration if available (~$20-30 USD). Learn to make traditional Costa Rican dishes like gallo pinto, arroz con leche, and tamales to recreate at home.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto, fresh fruit, and coffee at a local soda (~$4-6 USD)
meals.lunch: Snack at the hot springs or a packed lunch (~$4-7 USD)
meals.dinner: Dishes prepared during the cooking class or a simple soda meal (~$6-10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Public hot springs are significantly cheaper than resort-operated ones. Ask locals for directions to lesser-known spots. Always test water temperature before entering thermal pools.

day_by_day.morning: Spend your second-to-last full morning on a final eco-adventure activity. Consider white-water rafting on a nearby river (budget operators offer half-day trips for ~$45-65 USD) or a canopy walk through the rainforest treetops on suspension bridges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort and begin packing and organizing your belongings. Visit the local market one final time to pick up last-minute souvenirs such as local coffee, chocolate, handmade crafts, and spices - all affordable and authentic mementos.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a farewell dinner at your favorite local restaurant or soda from the trip. Reflect on your favorite memories and write in a travel journal. Take a final sunset beach walk.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast to fuel your last adventure (~$5-8 USD)
meals.lunch: Light snack at the activity base camp or market (~$4-7 USD)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at your favorite soda or local restaurant (~$9-14 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Budget for souvenirs in advance - local markets offer the best prices. Avoid airport gift shops which are significantly more expensive. Pack souvenirs securely in checked luggage.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one final sunrise on the beach. Take a last walk along the shoreline, breathe in the ocean air, and appreciate the incredible natural beauty of Costa Rica. Check out of the resort and settle any outstanding bills.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange your transfer back to Juan Santamaría International Airport via shared shuttle to keep costs low. Arrive at the airport with plenty of time for international departure. Browse duty-free shops if budget allows.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with incredible memories of eco-adventures, wildlife encounters, and the Pura Vida lifestyle. Review your photos and plan your next visit!

meals.breakfast: Final gallo pinto breakfast at a local soda or resort (~$4-6 USD)
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or pack snacks for the journey (~$6-10 USD)
meals.dinner: On the flight or at your destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in and security. Keep important documents, electronics, and valuables in your carry-on. Say Pura Vida to fellow travelers and staff as your final farewell!

trip_options.title: Classic Costa Rica Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the rainforest canopy on a thrilling multi-cable zip-line circuit with stunning views of Arenal Volcano. Experience the cloud forest ecosystem from above while spotting toucans, howler monkeys, and sloths along the way. Most operators include a hanging bridges walk as part of the package.
experiences.location: La Fortuna, Arenal Volcano National Park

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Night Walk
experiences.description: Explore the mystical Monteverde Cloud Forest after dark with a naturalist guide who uses spotlights to reveal nocturnal wildlife including kinkajous, glass frogs, tarantulas, sleeping birds, and the elusive olingo. The cloud forest takes on an entirely different character at night and offers a truly unforgettable eco-adventure experience.
experiences.location: Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve, Puntarenas Province

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight LH arrives at 13:00. No morning activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged shuttle transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort on the beachfront. Enjoy the scenic 2–3 hour drive, taking in your first views of Costa Rica's lush landscapes. Check in, freshen up, and explore the resort grounds and beach at leisure.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the beachfront at sunset to soak in your first Costa Rican evening. Enjoy a welcome cocktail at the resort bar before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in transit
meals.lunch: Light snack or meal at the airport or during transfer stop at a local soda (family-run Costa Rican diner) – try a classic Casado (rice, beans, plantains, and protein) for ~$8–12.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant – enjoy fresh seafood and local Costa Rican dishes. Budget ~$20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport shuttle in advance. Exchange some currency to Costa Rican Colones (CRC) at the airport. Keep luggage light and accessible for the transfer. February is dry season on most coasts – expect warm, sunny weather.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a guided beachfront sunrise walk and introductory wildlife spotting session along the resort's coastal area. Look for howler monkeys, scarlet macaws, and iguanas in the surrounding vegetation. A local naturalist guide can be arranged through the resort (~$25–35 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a nearby mangrove estuary for a kayaking or boat tour through the mangroves. Spot crocodiles, herons, kingfishers, and exotic bird species in their natural habitat. Tours typically last 2–3 hours and cost ~$40–55 per person.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a freshwater pool swim and relaxation. Enjoy happy hour at the beach bar before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the resort restaurant – gallo pinto (rice and beans), eggs, fresh tropical fruit, and Costa Rican coffee. ~$10–15.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or beachside snack bar near the mangrove tour departure point – fresh ceviche, patacones (fried plantains), and fruit juice. ~$10–14.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local beachfront restaurant near the resort – grilled whole fish (pargo), rice, and salad. ~$18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear reef-safe sunscreen and bring insect repellent for the mangrove tour. Binoculars are highly recommended for wildlife spotting. Book the mangrove tour the evening before through the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion begins: depart early by shuttle toward the Arenal Volcano region (approximately 3–4 hours depending on resort location). Enjoy the scenic drive through Costa Rica's Central Valley and agricultural highlands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in the Arenal area and check into a mid-range lodge or guesthouse for a 2-night stay (budget ~$60–90/night). After settling in, take a guided hike through Arenal Volcano National Park along the lava fields and primary rainforest trails. Spot toucans, coatis, and howler monkeys. Guided hike ~$30–45 per person.
day_by_day.evening: Unwind at the famous La Fortuna hot springs – choose from mid-range options like Eco Termales or Baldi Hot Springs (~$35–45 per person). Soak in volcanic mineral waters surrounded by jungle.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure – gallo pinto, toast, and coffee. ~$10–12.
meals.lunch: Stop at a local soda in La Fortuna town – try a Casado with chicken or fish. ~$8–12.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Don Rufino or a similar well-regarded La Fortuna restaurant – Costa Rican fusion cuisine with volcano views. ~$20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: This is a travel day – pack a day bag with essentials. Confirm shuttle booking 24 hours in advance. The Arenal area is lush and green year-round; light rain gear is recommended even in dry season. Book hot springs in advance as they fill up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: FEATURED EXPERIENCE – Arenal Volcano Zip-Line Canopy Tour: Soar through the rainforest canopy on a thrilling multi-cable zip-line circuit with stunning views of Arenal Volcano and Lake Arenal. The tour includes multiple cables, Tarzan swings, and hanging bridges (~$55–75 per person, approximately 3 hours). Depart by 8:00 AM for the best morning light and wildlife activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the zip-line tour, visit the Arenal Hanging Bridges for a self-guided or guided walk through the rainforest canopy walkways. Spot sloths, toucans, and poison dart frogs. Entry ~$24–30 per person. Alternatively, visit the La Fortuna Waterfall for a refreshing swim (~$18 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Return to La Fortuna for a leisurely evening. Browse the local artisan market for handmade crafts and souvenirs before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your lodge – included or available for ~$8–12. Eat well before the zip-line adventure.
meals.lunch: Post-zip-line lunch at a local café near the canopy tour base – sandwiches, fresh juice, and fruit. ~$10–14.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Nene's or a similar local family restaurant in La Fortuna – traditional Costa Rican cuisine, hearty portions. ~$15–22 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear closed-toe shoes and comfortable athletic clothing for the zip-line tour. Leave valuables at the lodge. Weight and age restrictions may apply – check in advance. Bring a small waterproof bag for the waterfall visit. Apply insect repellent before all outdoor activities.

day_by_day.morning: Morning wildlife boat tour on Lake Arenal or the Caño Negro Wildlife Refuge (if accessible). Spot caimans, river otters, roseate spoonbills, anhingas, and howler monkeys from the water. Tour duration ~3 hours, cost ~$45–65 per person including guide and transport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel by shuttle from La Fortuna to Monteverde (approximately 3–4 hours via the scenic Jeep-Boat-Jeep route across Lake Arenal – a classic Costa Rican adventure). Check into a mid-range Monteverde lodge or guesthouse (~$60–85/night).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the charming town of Santa Elena – browse local cheese shops (Monteverde is famous for its dairy), artisan stores, and coffee shops. Enjoy a relaxed evening settling into the cloud forest atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at La Fortuna lodge before departure – gallo pinto, eggs, fresh fruit, and coffee. ~$8–12.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a roadside soda during the Jeep-Boat-Jeep transfer. ~$8–12.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Morpho's Restaurant in Santa Elena – popular mid-range spot with excellent Costa Rican and international options. ~$16–24 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Jeep-Boat-Jeep transfer is an iconic Costa Rican experience and far more scenic than the road route. Book this transfer in advance through your lodge or a local agency (~$25–35 per person). Monteverde is cooler and mistier than Arenal – pack a light fleece or jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Morning guided walk through the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve – one of the world's most biodiverse ecosystems. Walk misty trails in search of the resplendent quetzal (February is prime quetzal season!), three-wattled bellbirds, and rare orchids. Guided tour ~$30–45 per person plus $25 reserve entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Butterfly Garden and/or the Monteverde Serpentarium for up-close wildlife encounters. Alternatively, explore the Hummingbird Gallery near the cloud forest entrance, where dozens of hummingbird species feed just inches away. Entry ~$10–15 per attraction.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the lodge before preparing for tonight's special experience.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the lodge – essential before the morning cloud forest walk. ~$8–12.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Colibri near the cloud forest reserve entrance – sandwiches, soups, and fresh coffee. ~$10–15.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tree House Restaurant in Santa Elena – unique dining inside a massive fig tree, great atmosphere and food. ~$18–26 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the Monteverde Reserve early (gates open at 7:00 AM) to maximize wildlife sightings before crowds arrive. Book a certified naturalist guide for the best quetzal-spotting chances. Wear layers – the cloud forest can be cool and wet even in dry season. Waterproof hiking boots strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning:
FEATURED EXPERIENCE – Monteverde Cloud Forest Night Walk: Explore the mystical Monteverde Cloud Forest after dark with a naturalist guide who uses spotlights to reveal nocturnal wildlife including kinkajous, sleeping birds, glass frogs, tarantulas, and olingo. (Note: This is an evening experience – schedule it for tonight. Morning is free for leisure or additional activities.)

Morning: Visit the Monteverde Coffee Tour at a local organic coffee farm. Learn about the coffee-growing process from seed to cup, and enjoy a tasting of some of the world's finest arabica coffee. Tour ~$25–35 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve – a less-visited alternative to the main Monteverde reserve with excellent wildlife and fewer crowds. Entry ~$15 plus optional guide ~$20. Look for emerald toucanets, squirrel cuckoos, and three-toed sloths.
day_by_day.evening: FEATURED EXPERIENCE – Monteverde Cloud Forest Night Walk: Depart at 5:30–6:00 PM with a naturalist guide for a 2-hour nocturnal forest experience. Discover the cloud forest's hidden nightlife – glass frogs, sleeping hummingbirds, kinkajous, and more. Cost ~$25–35 per person.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the lodge – gallo pinto, fresh fruit, and local Monteverde coffee. ~$8–12.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Sabor Tico in Santa Elena – authentic local cuisine, generous portions, excellent value. ~$10–14.
meals.dinner: Early dinner before the night walk at Tramonti Restaurant – Italian-Costa Rican fusion with cloud forest views. ~$18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The night walk requires closed-toe shoes and long pants (protection from insects and brush). Bring a small flashlight as backup. The naturalist guide's spotlight is the primary tool – avoid using phone flashlights as they disturb wildlife. Book the night walk at least one day in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Morning departure from Monteverde by shuttle toward the Pacific Coast (approximately 3–4 hours to the Guanacaste or Manuel Antonio area, depending on resort location). Enjoy the dramatic transition from misty cloud forest to sunny coastal lowlands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back at the Aegean Bliss Resort. Check back in, unpack, and spend the afternoon relaxing on the beachfront. Enjoy swimming, snorkeling, or paddleboarding in the calm Pacific waters.
day_by_day.evening: Beachside sunset watching followed by a leisurely dinner at the resort or a nearby local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Monteverde lodge before departure. ~$8–12.
meals.lunch: Stop at a local soda en route – try a fresh fish soup (sopa de mariscos) or Casado. ~$8–12.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant or a nearby beachfront spot – fresh grilled seafood platter. ~$20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: This is another travel day – pack light for the shuttle and enjoy the scenery. If your resort is near Manuel Antonio, consider booking activities in advance as it is a popular area. Confirm your shuttle booking 24 hours prior.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to a nearby national park (Manuel Antonio National Park or Carara National Park depending on resort location). Walk guided trails through primary rainforest and spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, sloths, scarlet macaws, and crocodiles. Park entry ~$18–20, guided tour ~$30–45.
day_by_day.afternoon: Beach time at the national park's pristine beaches (Manuel Antonio has some of Costa Rica's most beautiful beaches). Swim in calm waters, snorkel over coral reefs, and watch monkeys play in the beach-side trees. Pack snacks and water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a shower and rest. Enjoy the resort pool and bar before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before the park visit – essential to fuel the morning hike. ~$10–14.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or food from park-adjacent vendors – fresh coconut water, ceviche, and fruit. ~$8–12.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local restaurant near the resort – try La Luna (if near Manuel Antonio) or a similar mid-range coastal restaurant. ~$18–26 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the national park as early as possible (opens at 7:00 AM) to beat crowds and maximize wildlife sightings. Monkeys are bold and may approach – do not feed them. Secure all food in your bag. Bring reef-safe sunscreen for beach time.

day_by_day.morning: Guided snorkeling or stand-up paddleboard (SUP) tour along the coastal reef. Explore underwater marine life including tropical fish, sea turtles, rays, and colorful coral formations. Snorkel tour ~$45–65 per person including equipment and guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local wildlife rescue and rehabilitation center (such as Kids Saving the Rainforest or a similar center near your resort). Learn about Costa Rica's conservation efforts and see rescued sloths, monkeys, birds, and reptiles up close. Entry/donation ~$15–25.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset catamaran cruise along the Pacific Coast – enjoy sailing, dolphin watching, snorkeling stops, and a light snack on board. Cost ~$65–85 per person. Book in advance.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort – fresh tropical fruit bowl, granola, yogurt, and coffee. ~$10–14.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beachside soda near the snorkel tour departure – fresh fish tacos, patacones, and agua fresca. ~$10–15.
meals.dinner: Light dinner after the catamaran cruise – snacks may be included on the boat. Stop at a local pizzeria or casual restaurant near the resort. ~$15–20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The catamaran sunset cruise is a highlight – book early as spots fill quickly in February (dry season peak). Bring a light layer for the boat as ocean breezes can be cool after sunset. The wildlife rescue center visit is both educational and emotionally rewarding – a must for wildlife enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: Half-day white-water rafting excursion on a nearby river (Río Savegre or Río Naranjo are popular options near the central Pacific coast). Choose Class II–III rapids for a fun, accessible adventure suitable for most fitness levels. Tour ~$65–85 per person including transport, guide, equipment, and snack.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a relaxed afternoon. Enjoy the beachfront, resort pool, or treat yourself to a massage or spa treatment at the resort (~$50–80 for a 60-minute massage). This is a well-deserved rest afternoon after an active morning.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local town or village near the resort – browse artisan markets, pick up handmade souvenirs (look for wooden carvings, leather goods, and locally made chocolate), and enjoy the local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hearty breakfast at the resort before rafting – eggs, gallo pinto, toast, and coffee. ~$10–14.
meals.lunch: Post-rafting lunch included with most tour packages, or stop at a local soda for a Casado. ~$8–12.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local mid-range restaurant in town – try a traditional Costa Rican meal of arroz con pollo (chicken with rice) or fresh sea bass (corvina). ~$16–22 per person.

day_by_day.notes: White-water rafting requires moderate physical fitness. Wear a swimsuit under quick-dry clothing and secure all valuables at the base camp. The Río Savegre is also known for excellent bird watching along its banks – keep an eye out for kingfishers and herons during the raft trip.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching tour with a local ornithologist guide. The Pacific coastal lowlands are home to hundreds of bird species including scarlet macaws, toucans, motmots, and tanagers. Tour ~$40–55 per person (2–3 hours). Bring binoculars.
day_by_day.afternoon: Free afternoon for personal exploration. Options include: horseback riding on the beach (~$45–60), visiting a local waterfall for swimming, exploring tide pools at low tide, or simply relaxing on the beach with a good book. Check resort activity board for additional options.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner – splurge slightly on a nicer restaurant for a memorable final full evening. Enjoy fresh Costa Rican lobster or a seafood platter with a local craft beer or glass of Chilean wine.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before birdwatching – granola, yogurt, and coffee. ~$8–10.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the resort or a beachside café – ceviche, fresh coconut, and fruit plate. ~$12–16.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the best restaurant near the resort – budget ~$30–45 per person for a special meal. Look for a restaurant with ocean views for the perfect send-off.

day_by_day.notes: This is your last full day in Costa Rica – make the most of it! Consider picking up any remaining souvenirs today. Pack non-essential items in the evening to make tomorrow morning's departure smoother. Confirm your airport transfer booking for tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Costa Rica. Wake up early for one last sunrise walk on the beach – a peaceful and reflective way to end the trip. Take photos, collect a few shells, and say goodbye to the Pacific Ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Board your pre-arranged shuttle transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport. Allow 3–4 hours for transfer plus check-in and security. Enjoy the final views of Costa Rica's beautiful landscapes on the drive.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with incredible memories of rainforests, volcanoes, wildlife, and adventure. ¡Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the resort – enjoy one last gallo pinto, fresh tropical fruit, and Costa Rican coffee. ~$10–14.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or during a transfer stop – grab a final casado or a bocas (appetizers) at an airport café. ~$10–15.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM – confirm with the resort. Allow ample time for the airport transfer, especially on weekends when traffic can be heavier. Keep your passport, flight documents, and a small amount of CRC easily accessible. Declare any agricultural products at customs. Consider purchasing locally made coffee or chocolate at the airport as final gifts or souvenirs.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the rainforest canopy on a thrilling multi-cable zip-line circuit with stunning views of Arenal Volcano. Experience the cloud forest ecosystem from above while spotting toucans, howler monkeys, and sloths along the way. Most operators include a hanging bridges walk as part of the package.
experiences.location: La Fortuna, Arenal Volcano National Park

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari, spotting caimans, river turtles, poison dart frogs, manatees, and an extraordinary variety of tropical birds. If visiting between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of endangered green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Night Walk
experiences.description: Explore the mystical Monteverde Cloud Forest after dark with a naturalist guide who uses spotlights to reveal nocturnal wildlife including kinkajous, glass frogs, tarantulas, sleeping birds, and the elusive olingo. The cloud forest takes on an entirely different character at night and offers a truly unforgettable eco-adventure experience.
experiences.location: Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve, Puntarenas Province

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio Beach and Rainforest Combo Day
experiences.description: Spend a day in Manuel Antonio National Park where pristine white-sand beaches meet lush rainforest teeming with wildlife. Spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, three-toed sloths, and scarlet macaws just steps from the turquoise Pacific waters. Hire a local guide for two hours to maximize wildlife sightings, then relax on Playa Manuel Antonio afterward.

experiences.name: Cacao Farm Tour and Traditional Costa Rican Cooking Class
experiences.description: Visit a working organic cacao farm to learn the full bean-to-bar chocolate-making process used by indigenous Bribri communities for centuries. Follow the tour with a hands-on cooking class preparing traditional Costa Rican dishes such as gallo pinto, casado, and plantain-based recipes using locally sourced ingredients. A rich cultural and culinary immersion in one experience.
experiences.location: Puerto Viejo de Talamanca, Caribbean South Coast

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Private luxury transfer from Juan Santamaría International Airport to Aegean Bliss Resort arranged with a personal concierge greeting at arrivals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private resort welcome experience: guided orientation tour of the Aegean Bliss Resort grounds, beachfront suite check-in with champagne welcome amenity, and a leisurely first exploration of the resort's private beach and infinity pool. Settle in and decompress from travel.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour at the resort's oceanfront bar, followed by a relaxed welcome dinner at the resort's signature restaurant. Time to orient with the concierge to confirm upcoming experiences and any personal preferences.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or at airport — no resort breakfast on Day 1
meals.lunch: Light snack or refreshments provided in private transfer vehicle or upon arrival at resort (pre-arranged welcome platter in suite)
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort Signature Restaurant — multi-course Costa Rican fusion tasting menu featuring fresh ceviche, hearts of palm salad, grilled sea bass with plantain purée, and locally sourced tropical fruit desserts paired with premium Costa Rican craft cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Confirm all upcoming excursion bookings with the resort concierge this evening. Request an early morning wake-up call for Day 2. Unpack and rest — no strenuous activities on arrival day. Ensure travel documents, passports, and experience vouchers are organized.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely resort morning — enjoy a gourmet breakfast at the beachfront terrace restaurant. Followed by a private guided nature walk along the resort's coastal trail with a resident naturalist, spotting local birds, iguanas, and coastal flora unique to Costa Rica's Pacific beachfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private resort experience: luxury kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding session along the calm coastal waters arranged through the resort's water sports concierge. Alternatively, enjoy a premium snorkeling excursion to a nearby reef with a private guide and all equipment provided.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails on the private beach with a curated charcuterie and ceviche board. Dinner at a highly-rated local fine dining restaurant near the resort, celebrating the first full day in Costa Rica.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort beachfront terrace — full gourmet breakfast with tropical fruit platters, eggs Benedict with smoked marlin, fresh-pressed juices, and Costa Rican specialty coffee (Café Britt or Tarrazú single-origin)
meals.lunch: Light beach club lunch at the resort — grilled shrimp tacos, fresh coconut agua fresca, and ceviche de corvina
meals.dinner: Premium local restaurant near resort — whole grilled snapper, traditional casado with black beans and rice, plantains, and a bottle of premium Chilean or Argentine Malbec

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle acclimatization day. The Pacific coast weather in February is typically dry season with sunny skies and low humidity — ideal beach weather. Apply reef-safe sunscreen for all water activities. Hydration is essential in the tropical climate.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Manuel Antonio National Park — depart resort early by private luxury 4x4 vehicle with a personal naturalist guide. Morning entry into the park (one of Costa Rica's most biodiverse) for a guided rainforest hike spotting white-faced capuchin monkeys, three-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and coatis along well-maintained jungle trails.
day_by_day.afternoon: Manuel Antonio Beach and Rainforest Combo Day experience continues — transition from rainforest to the park's pristine white-sand beaches (Playa Manuel Antonio). Enjoy a private beachside picnic lunch prepared by the resort, swim in turquoise waters, and snorkel in the protected marine area. Optional: guided tidepooling with the naturalist.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by private transfer. Freshen up and enjoy a spa treatment at the resort's wellness center (deep tissue massage or rainforest botanical wrap recommended after a full hiking day). Dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early departure breakfast at resort — grab-and-go gourmet box prepared by the resort kitchen: artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, granola parfait, and thermos of specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Private gourmet picnic on Playa Manuel Antonio — curated by resort chef with cold-pressed juices, tropical fruit, chilled shrimp cocktail, artisan wraps, and coconut water
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort — poolside dining experience with grilled lobster tail, mango salsa, roasted vegetables, and a premium Costa Rican craft beer or wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park has a daily visitor cap — ensure entry tickets are pre-booked by the resort concierge well in advance. Wear lightweight moisture-wicking clothing, sturdy hiking sandals or trail shoes, and bring insect repellent. Binoculars are essential for wildlife spotting.

day_by_day.morning: Cacao Farm Tour and Traditional Costa Rican Cooking Class experience — depart by private transfer to a working organic cacao farm. Begin with a guided walking tour of the cacao plantation, learning the full bean-to-bar chocolate-making process from harvest to fermentation, drying, roasting, and grinding. Sample artisan dark chocolates at various stages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Traditional Costa Rican cooking class continues on the farm — work alongside a local chef to prepare authentic dishes: gallo pinto, tamales, arroz con leche, and traditional Caribbean-style rice and beans with coconut milk. Enjoy the prepared meal together in a beautiful open-air rancho setting on the farm.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Enjoy the resort's beach club for sunset. Opt for a private couples' or solo dining experience on the beach — a candlelit table set directly on the sand with personalized menu and sommelier service.

meals.breakfast: Resort terrace breakfast — açaí bowls, smoked salmon on cassava toast, tropical fruit, and Costa Rican pour-over coffee
meals.lunch: Included as part of the Cacao Farm cooking class — the dishes prepared during the class form the afternoon meal, served with fresh lemonade and tropical juices in the farm's rancho
meals.dinner: Private candlelit beach dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — curated 5-course tasting menu with wine pairing: tuna tataki, hearts of palm bisque, grilled wagyu beef tenderloin with chimichurri, local cheese board, and passion fruit soufflé

day_by_day.notes: The cacao farm experience is hands-on and immersive — wear comfortable clothes you don't mind getting a little dirty. This is a culturally rich day that connects guests deeply with Costa Rican agricultural heritage. Purchase artisan chocolate products from the farm as premium souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Resort wellness morning — begin with a sunrise yoga session on the beachfront deck led by the resort's private yoga instructor. Follow with a guided meditation and breathwork session. Enjoy a healthy spa breakfast afterward at the wellness pavilion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Aerial tram or private canopy walkway experience near the resort area — visit a nearby private nature reserve offering suspended bridge canopy walks through primary rainforest, with a naturalist guide identifying tropical birds (toucans, parrots, tanagers), insects, and plant life from above the forest floor.
day_by_day.evening: Resort social evening — join the resort's weekly premium cultural event (live marimba music, traditional dance performance, and Costa Rican rum and craft spirits tasting). Dinner at the resort's beach bar with a festive atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Wellness breakfast at resort spa pavilion — green smoothie bowls, avocado toast on sourdough, poached eggs, herbal teas, and cold-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Resort beach club — fresh ceviche bar with multiple preparations (classic, mango-habanero, coconut-lime), grilled fish skewers, and cold tropical beverages
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort beach bar — casual premium dining: wood-fired pizza with local toppings, mixed seafood platter, craft cocktails featuring Costa Rican guaro and fresh tropical ingredients

day_by_day.notes: This is a lighter activity day designed as a mid-trip recovery day before the more adventurous experiences ahead. Take time to explore the resort's full amenity offering — private pool, spa facilities, gym, and beach. February evenings on the Pacific coast are warm and perfect for outdoor cultural events.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private luxury vehicle for the journey toward the Arenal Volcano region (approximately 3–4 hours from the Pacific coast). Enjoy the scenic drive through Costa Rica's interior highlands with a comfort stop at a local coffee cooperative for a premium coffee tasting and farm tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at a luxury lodge near Arenal for a one-night stay (pre-booked premium lodge with volcano views — e.g., Nayara Springs or Tabacón Grand Spa Thermal Resort). Check in and enjoy the natural thermal hot springs fed by the Arenal Volcano's geothermal energy. Relax in private thermal pools surrounded by rainforest.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views of Arenal Volcano from the lodge terrace (weather permitting). Dinner at the lodge's fine dining restaurant with volcano panorama views.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast at Aegean Bliss before departure — continental spread with pastries, fruit, and coffee to go
meals.lunch: Gourmet stop en route — La Fortuna town's best restaurant for traditional Costa Rican lunch: sopa negra (black bean soup), chifrijo, and fresh tropical juices
meals.dinner: Arenal lodge fine dining restaurant — volcano-view dinner featuring Costa Rican highland cuisine: slow-braised beef short rib, yuca gratin, local vegetable medley, and artisan desserts with premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: This is a travel transition day. Confirm the Arenal lodge reservation has been pre-arranged by the resort concierge. Pack an overnight bag for the Arenal excursion — luggage can be stored at Aegean Bliss if needed. The thermal hot springs are best enjoyed in the evening when the cooler air temperature creates a magical atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Arenal Volcano Zip-Line Canopy Tour — the flagship adventure experience. Depart early to a premium zip-line operator near Arenal (e.g., Sky Trek or Arenal Mundo Aventura). Soar through the rainforest canopy on a multi-cable zip-line circuit with stunning views of Arenal Volcano, Lake Arenal, and the surrounding jungle. Includes up to 11 cables, hanging bridges, and Tarzan swings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post zip-line adrenaline wind-down: guided hanging bridges walk through the Arenal rainforest with a naturalist, spotting poison dart frogs, howler monkeys, toucans, and morpho butterflies. Return to the thermal lodge for a final soak in the private thermal pools.
day_by_day.evening: Private transfer back to Aegean Bliss Resort on the Pacific coast (3–4 hours). Arrive in time for a late dinner at the resort. Celebrate the mid-trip adventure milestone.

meals.breakfast: Arenal lodge — full hot breakfast before the zip-line adventure: eggs any style, Costa Rican gallo pinto, fresh fruit, and strong local coffee
meals.lunch: Post-adventure lunch at the zip-line operator's on-site restaurant or a nearby La Fortuna café — casado plate with grilled chicken, rice, beans, salad, and plantains
meals.dinner: Late arrival dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — lighter fare: premium sushi and sashimi platter, miso soup, edamame, and Japanese whisky or sake (resort's fusion menu option)

day_by_day.notes: The Arenal Volcano Zip-Line Canopy Tour requires participants to meet minimum weight and health requirements — confirm with the operator in advance. Wear closed-toe shoes, long pants recommended, and secure all loose items. GoPro cameras can often be rented from the operator for an additional fee. The return drive is scenic but long — bring snacks and entertainment.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery morning at Aegean Bliss Resort after the Arenal adventure days. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and spend the morning at the resort's private beach or infinity pool. Optional: private surf lesson on the resort's beach with a professional instructor (Costa Rica's Pacific coast offers excellent beginner to intermediate surf conditions in February).
day_by_day.afternoon: Private sport fishing charter — depart from the nearest marina for a half-day deep-sea fishing excursion. Target species include sailfish, mahi-mahi, and roosterfish (catch-and-release or keep for resort preparation). Fully equipped luxury fishing vessel with captain, first mate, and all premium tackle included.
day_by_day.evening: If fish was kept from the charter, arrange a 'catch-to-table' dinner experience with the resort chef — your fresh catch prepared to your specifications. Otherwise, enjoy the resort's premium seafood restaurant for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — eggs Benedict with hollandaise, smoked fish, tropical fruit platter, pastries, and specialty coffee. Taken slowly and leisurely at the beachfront terrace
meals.lunch: On the fishing boat — premium packed lunch prepared by resort: gourmet sandwiches, fresh fruit, energy bars, and cold beverages including craft beers
meals.dinner: Catch-to-table experience at Aegean Bliss — your fresh-caught fish (or resort's market fish) prepared ceviche-style as starter, followed by grilled whole fish with garlic butter, roasted vegetables, and a premium Burgundy white wine

day_by_day.notes: Deep-sea fishing charters must be booked in advance through the resort concierge. February is excellent fishing season on Costa Rica's Pacific coast — sailfish are particularly active. Apply high-SPF sunscreen and bring polarized sunglasses and a hat for the fishing charter. Seasickness medication recommended if sensitive.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure by private charter flight or luxury ground transfer to Tortuguero on Costa Rica's Caribbean coast (a significant journey — charter flight recommended for premium experience, approximately 45 minutes vs. 5–6 hours by road). Check into a premium eco-lodge in Tortuguero (e.g., Tortuga Lodge & Gardens or Manatus Hotel).
day_by_day.afternoon: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari — the signature Caribbean coast experience. Glide through the intricate jungle canal network of Tortuguero on a private guided boat safari. Spot caimans basking on riverbanks, river turtles sunning on logs, Jesus Christ lizards running across the water's surface, river otters, manatees (occasionally), and an extraordinary array of tropical birds including kingfishers, herons, and toucans.
day_by_day.evening: Tortuguero village walk — explore the small, colorful Caribbean village of Tortuguero (accessible only by boat or plane) with a local guide. Learn about the community's conservation efforts and turtle protection programs. Dinner at the eco-lodge's restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at Aegean Bliss before departure — continental spread and coffee to go
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at Tortuguero eco-lodge upon arrival — Caribbean-style rice and beans with coconut milk, jerk chicken, fresh tropical fruit, and cold Pilsen beer
meals.dinner: Tortuguero eco-lodge fine dining — Caribbean fusion cuisine: coconut curry shrimp, breadfruit gratin, plantain tostones, and rum cake with tropical fruit compote

day_by_day.notes: A private charter flight to Tortuguero is strongly recommended for a premium experience — the journey by road and boat is lengthy and tiring. February is not sea turtle nesting season (nesting peaks July–October for green turtles), but the park's wildlife and canal system are spectacular year-round. Pack light for the Tortuguero overnight — bring insect repellent, rain jacket, and waterproof bag for boat safari.

day_by_day.morning: Dawn wildlife boat safari in Tortuguero — the early morning hours (5:30–7:30 AM) are the best time for wildlife activity in the canals. Second guided boat excursion focusing on bird life and amphibians, including red-eyed tree frogs, poison dart frogs, and early-rising river wildlife. Photography-focused with a naturalist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return charter flight to the Pacific coast / resort area. Afternoon at leisure at Aegean Bliss Resort — decompress by the pool or beach after the Caribbean adventure. Optional: resort spa treatment (hot stone massage or tropical botanical body treatment).
day_by_day.evening: Romantic or celebratory dinner at the resort — premium private dining experience in a secluded garden or beachfront setting, arranged with advance notice to the resort's events team.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn light snack at eco-lodge before morning safari — coffee, fruit, and pastries. Full breakfast upon return from morning boat tour: Caribbean scrambled eggs, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: In-flight snack or light meal at airport lounge during transfer, or early lunch at Tortuguero lodge before departure
meals.dinner: Private garden dining at Aegean Bliss Resort — 6-course chef's table experience with wine pairing: amuse-bouche, lobster bisque, micro-green salad, sea bass en papillote, wagyu beef medallion, and passion fruit crème brûlée

day_by_day.notes: The dawn boat safari requires a very early wake-up — confirm the 5:30 AM departure time with the eco-lodge the evening before. Bring a headlamp and warm layer for the early morning on the water. The return charter flight should be booked for late morning to allow time for the morning safari. Keep the afternoon genuinely relaxed — two days of travel and adventure require recovery.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Night Walk preparation day — depart by private luxury vehicle for the Monteverde region (approximately 3–4 hours from the Pacific coast). En route, stop at a premium birdwatching reserve in the Nicoya Peninsula area for a guided morning birdwatching session with a specialist ornithologist guide, targeting resplendent quetzals, motmots, and trogons.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive Monteverde — check into a luxury cloud forest lodge (e.g., El Silencio Lodge & Spa or Monteverde Lodge & Gardens). Afternoon at leisure: explore the lodge's private cloud forest trails, visit the famous Monteverde Cheese Factory (a local institution), or enjoy the lodge's spa and wellness facilities.
day_by_day.evening: Monteverde Cloud Forest Night Walk — the mystical signature experience. Join a small-group (or private) guided night walk through the cloud forest with an expert naturalist using high-powered spotlights to reveal the forest's nocturnal world: kinkajous, sleeping birds, glass frogs, tarantulas, stick insects, and the magical glow of bioluminescent fungi.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort — early departure breakfast: full hot breakfast with gallo pinto, eggs, tropical fruit, and coffee before the drive
meals.lunch: En route lunch stop in Santa Elena (Monteverde's gateway town) — Santa Elena's best restaurant serving traditional Costa Rican fare: sopa de mariscos, fresh-baked bread, and local cheese
meals.dinner: Post-night-walk dinner at Monteverde cloud forest lodge — highland comfort cuisine: mushroom risotto with local cloud forest fungi, braised lamb, root vegetable medley, and a warming glass of premium Costa Rican dark rum

day_by_day.notes: The Monteverde Cloud Forest Night Walk is best experienced as a private tour — request this through the concierge for an exclusive experience with a dedicated naturalist. Wear dark-colored, long-sleeved clothing and closed-toe shoes for the night walk. Temperatures in Monteverde's cloud forest can drop to 15–18°C at night — bring a light fleece or jacket. Silence is key for wildlife encounters.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve — early morning guided hike through the primary cloud forest reserve at dawn, when mist hangs between the ancient trees and bird activity peaks. With a private naturalist guide, explore the reserve's famous hanging bridges and look for the legendary resplendent quetzal (February is the beginning of quetzal breeding season — excellent sighting opportunity).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return private transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort on the Pacific coast (3–4 hours). Arrive mid-afternoon for final resort days. Penultimate afternoon at the beach — soak in the Pacific sunset, swim, and enjoy the resort's beach club facilities. Optional: final surf session or paddleboarding.
day_by_day.evening: Premium farewell pre-dinner experience: private sunset catamaran cruise along the Pacific coastline with champagne, canapés, and a professional photographer to capture the final Costa Rica sunset. Return to resort for a memorable farewell dinner.

meals.breakfast: Monteverde lodge — cloud forest breakfast with panoramic misty views: fresh-baked pastries, local cheese platter, scrambled eggs with cloud forest mushrooms, and specialty highland coffee
meals.lunch: En route lunch — roadside soda (traditional Costa Rican eatery) for an authentic local experience: casado with fresh-caught tilapia, rice, beans, salad, and fresh fruit agua fresca
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's finest restaurant — premium tasting menu celebrating 13 days in Costa Rica: local oysters, tuna carpaccio, lobster thermidor, filet mignon with truffle butter, artisan cheese board, and a decadent chocolate fondant with Costa Rican cacao ganache, paired with a premium Champagne toast

day_by_day.notes: The sunset catamaran cruise should be pre-booked through the resort concierge — February sunsets on the Pacific coast are spectacular and the calm dry-season seas make for ideal sailing conditions. Request the professional photographer service in advance. This is the second-to-last night — take time to reflect on the journey and collect any remaining souvenirs or artisan products from the resort boutique.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Aegean Bliss Resort — wake up naturally and enjoy a slow, luxurious final breakfast at the beachfront terrace. Take a last walk on the private beach, collect any final memories, and complete check-out formalities. The resort concierge will arrange luggage handling and final packing of any purchased items.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time — either a final resort activity (spa treatment, pool, or beach) or private luxury transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport in San José. Concierge to arrange VIP airport assistance, fast-track check-in, and access to the premium airport lounge.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Costa Rica — board flight home with extraordinary memories of 13 days of eco-adventure, wildlife, and luxury in one of the world's most biodiverse countries.

meals.breakfast: Grand final breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — the full luxury spread: made-to-order eggs, smoked fish, tropical fruit extravaganza, pastry basket, specialty Costa Rican coffee, and fresh-pressed juices. Savored slowly with a view of the Pacific
meals.lunch: Airport premium lounge lunch or an early lunch at a fine restaurant near the airport in San José if time permits — traditional Costa Rican farewell meal
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination — the resort can arrange a premium picnic box or gourmet travel meal for the journey home

day_by_day.notes: Allow a minimum of 3 hours before international departure for airport procedures in San José. The resort concierge should confirm the exact transfer departure time based on the return flight schedule. Ensure all purchased artisan goods, chocolates, coffee, and souvenirs are properly packed — declare any food items at customs as required. Costa Rica has strict agricultural export rules. Consider purchasing premium Costa Rican coffee, artisan chocolate, and handcrafted items as final gifts from the resort boutique.

query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami
